To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
transparent PI nanocomposite films containing different diamine monomers were synthesized and characterized.
transparent polyimide nanocomposites containing 0.5 wt% organoclay exhibited improved thermo-mechanical and optical transparency properties compared with the neat polyimide.

the addition of organically modified montmorillonite (Cloisite 30 B) into polyimide (6FDA-BAS) and (6FDA-BASH) films resulted in a decrease in the optical transparency and thermal properties, while the glass transition temperature and mechanical properties were enhanced.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of transparent PI/organoclay nanocomposite films.
the synthesis of transparent nanocomposites containing organically modified clay.
the synthesis and characterization of transparent polyimides containing organoclay.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PI hybrid films containing organoclay were superior to the pure PI films.
the PI hybrid films containing BAS monomer and 0.5 wt% organoclay have the best thermal stability, mechanical properties, and optical transparency.
the properties of PI hybrids can be improved by the addition of -OH groups to the diamines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PI hybrids synthesized using the BAS monomer were better than those synthesized using the BAS-OH monomer.
the properties of PI hybrid films are affected by the diamine monomer and the amount of organoclay.
BAS PI hybrids were more suitable than the BAS-OH hybrids as transparent polyimide nanocomposite films.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BAS PI hybrids are better suited for optical applications, and the BAS-OH hybrids are better for mechanical applications.
the PI nanocomposite films containing organically modified clay have potential for applications in the field of optoelectronic materials.
